To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) domain generalization can be achieved by synthesizing novel domains implicitly, which increase domain diversity and thus the generalizability; (b) such synthesis can be achieved by mixing styles of training instances, which is easy and efficient to perform in mini-batch training.

1) domain generalization can be improved by mixing style statistics of training samples; 2) our approach, termed MixStyle and based on probabilistically style-mixing, is easy to implement, and 3) MixStyle is effective for a wide range of visual tasks

(i) domain generalization can be achieved with simple instance-level feature mixing across domains; (ii) such feature mixing can be implemented in mini-batch training, and (iii) the proposed method can be easily applied to various tasks including reinforcement learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make a neural network more domain generalizable.
how to improve generalization of deep neural network models.

the following questions: How can we improve the generalization ability of a CNN? Can we improve a model's generalization ability by mixing styles of training instances? How to mix styles of training instances to achieve better domain generalization? How to apply our proposed method to reinforcement learning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper is well written, the proposed method is simple, effective and easy to implement.
MixStyle is simple and effective, and it outperforms state-of-the-art domain generalization approaches by a large margin on various benchmarks.
MixStyle can be used to improve generalization performance in various domains, such as image, text, and reinforcement learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a simple yet effective approach, MixStyle, for domain generalization.
MixStyle is able to improve generalization ability of a CNN on both seen and unseen domains.
MixStyle is a simple yet effective method for domain generalization, which can be readily used in various applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
domain generalization is a natural consequence of learning to mix style.
mixing style information of training instances across domains can help CNNs generalize better to novel domains, which is a simple yet effective way for improving domain generalization.
, for domain generalization, the domain gap is better bridged by mixing styles of training samples than by mixing training instances directly.
